html:
An encyclopedia in 37 books by Pliny the Elder, finished around 77 CE and dedicated to the future emperor Titus. It is the largest single work to survive from the Roman Empire.

Pliny meant it to cover "the natural world, or life". It moves from the universe and the stars through geography and peoples, animals, plants, farming, medicine, and finally metals and stones. Those last books include a history of Greek and Roman painting and sculpture, a main source for ancient art. In his preface Pliny says he collected 20,000 facts from about a hundred authors, among them Cato's book on farming.

He mixes careful observation with travellers' tales: peoples with one leg or no mouths sit beside precise notes on how to make glass or grow olives. He also complains about Roman luxury, such as the gold and silk imported from the east.

Monks copied it throughout the Middle Ages, and it was one of the first classical books printed, in Venice in 1469. It became a model for later encyclopedias and stayed a standard reference into the Renaissance. Pliny died two years after finishing it, in the eruption of Vesuvius.
sum: An encyclopedia in 37 books by Pliny the Elder, finished around 77 CE and dedicated to the future emperor Titus. It is the largest single work to survive from the Roman Empire.
